The first tagged release of goant, a JavaScript engine in pure Go.

No cgo, nothing fetched at build time, one static binary, and it cross-compiles
wherever Go does. Built for [Robomotion](https://www.robomotion.io), where it
runs customer JavaScript inside production RPA robots.

## What is in it

- **99.4% of Test262**, with nothing excluded. Not a profile and not a subset:
  `goant-t262 -all` runs every file in the suite. 53,247 of 53,573.
- **ES2025**, including modules, `Temporal`, and `Intl` with its own CLDR data.
- **A baseline JIT** for amd64 and arm64, with inline caches, type feedback for
  element access, direct compiled-to-compiled calls and mid-function
  deoptimization. Worth 3.1x over the fifteen Octane workloads.
- **A Go-idiomatic embedding API**: `Runtime`, `Scope`, `Pool`, `Value`, a
  tracing collector, and a memory limit that reports an error rather than
  aborting the process. See [docs/embedding.md](https://github.com/robomotionio/goant/blob/main/docs/embedding.md).

## The binaries here

The `goant` CLI, for six platforms. It runs the compiled tier by default;
`goant -jit=false` turns it off, and `goant --version` says which build you have.

| platform | asset |
|---|---|
| linux amd64 | `goant-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` |
| linux arm64 | `goant-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` |
| macOS intel | `goant-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` |
| macOS apple silicon | `goant-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` |
| windows amd64 | `goant-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.zip` |
| windows arm64 | `goant-aarch64-pc-windows-gnu.zip` |

To embed the package instead:

```sh
go get github.com/robomotionio/goant
```

There is also a rolling [`nightly`](https://github.com/robomotionio/goant/releases/tag/nightly)
prerelease built from the head of `main`.

## Worth knowing before you depend on it

The JIT is **off by default when you embed the package** and on in the CLI. The
two answer different questions, and the reasoning is in the README.

A deliberately hostile script can still outrun the memory limit and the
deadline, by handing a generic array built-in a length no real array can have.
Ordinary code, including ordinary runaway code, is bounded. The cases that could
end the process are fixed and have tests keeping them that way. The
[Status](https://github.com/robomotionio/goant#status) section says exactly what
is left.
